lifecycle.ready_for_validation_summary: MT-135 implemented. MECHANISM (AC-135-2, generalises without an allowlist): egui 0.33.3 keeps AT MOST ONE open popup per viewport - a single OpenPopup{id,pos} slot in egui::Memory. Top menu-bar dropdowns, pane/tab/tree/editor context menus and any future Popup::menu / Popup::context_menu / Popup::open_memory caller all funnel through that one slot, so copying it projects EVERY memory-backed popup surface, present and future, with no registration step for a new menu. egui exposes no public 'which popup is open' getter (Memory::popups is private), so the new module accessibility/popup_projection.rs composes two public halves: Memory::areas().visible_layer_ids() (an open popup always has a visible layer, because Popup::show renders through Area::new(popup_id)) probed by Popup::is_id_open for exact match. Only one can match, so the unordered HashSet cannot make it nondeterministic. The stored POSITION is load-bearing, not polish: Popup::context_menu uses PopupAnchor::PointerFixed, so re-opening without the position yields anchor.rect == None and egui SILENTLY RENDERS NOTHING - a position-less projection would have looked like a fix while publishing nothing. WHY THE MT-121 COORDINATE CONTRACT SURVIVES (AC-135-3): only egui::Id + Option<Pos2> crosses the context boundary. No focus, no Memory::data (where scroll offsets and widget state live), no area geometry, no interaction state. The blanket Memory clone that the contract's red-team flagged is explicitly rejected in the module docs. Proven rather than asserted: published and rendered bounds for the menu leaf matched with ZERO delta - published=(x=381.000, y=286.000, w=586.000, h=18.000) rendered=(x=381.000, y=286.000, w=586.000, h=18.000) - and the whole-tree viewport guard was re-run WITH a menu projected. The MT-121 theme-toggle proof is unchanged and still exact. PT-135-1 RED (verbatim): 3 tests failed, including the inverted witness - "AC-135-1: 'ctx-menu.pane.pop_out' is open in the live rendered frame, so it MUST appear in the published MCP snapshot". PT-135-1 GREEN (verbatim): 'test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed'. PT-135-3 CLOSED-MENU PROOF (AC-135-5) checks two closed states that fail differently: never-opened (a projection that force-opened menus would publish it) and opened-then-dismissed-with-Escape (a latching or stale projection would keep publishing a menu the operator dismissed). Runtime line: never_opened=false while_open=true after_escape=false. Stale entries cannot leak because Memory::end_pass drops any popup not kept open during the pass and the projection is read fresh per capture, never cached. PT-135-4 REGRESSION: native lib suite 2074 passed / 0 failed (the MT-121 baseline was 2069; +4 are this MT's unit tests and +1 predates it, which the implementer recorded as NOT_INSPECTED rather than guessing). Ten targeted integration binaries green including test_context_menu, test_context_menu_surfaces and test_menu_wireup. Implementer evidence only, not validation.
ready_for_validation_v4_open_items: SUBMENUS NOT_INSPECTED: one-level submenus (ui.menu_button) keep MenuState in Memory::data, which is deliberately not projected, so an open SUBMENU may not render in the capture pass. The parent menu and its items do. No acceptance criterion covers this and it was not proven either way.

Menu-internal keyboard cursor is not projected: render_menu_root stores its highlight index in Memory::data. Item identity, bounds and clickability are correct, but a model reading tree-focus inside an open menu sees the first actionable item rather than the operator's arrowed-to item. Fixing it means copying Memory::data, which is the exact layout risk this MT rejected.

A popup opened in memory but never rendered in a live frame is not in visible_layer_ids() and will not project. Not currently reachable, since context_menu::request_open is followed by a live frame, but it is a real edge; the mcp_open_top_menu forward projection covers the equivalent case for top menus only.

No GPU-pixel proof was run. AC-135-3 is proven against the live AccessKit tree - the same tree the platform UIA adapter receives - with an exact zero-delta match, and the contract's gui_obligation accepts accesskit-tree evidence. The real-GPU path is available on this host if a validator wants pixels.

scope.summary: HandshakeApp::refresh_mcp_snapshot builds a BRAND-NEW egui::Context for the model-vision capture pass. That fresh context has an EMPTY egui::Memory, so any surface whose open/closed state lives in egui::Memory is absent from the published MCP snapshot even when it is visibly open in the live window. app.rs already works around this for two surfaces by hand-copying the Reading-mode store and the open top-menu into the capture context, but pointer-opened PANE CONTEXT MENUS have no such projection. Consequence: a model driving Argus cannot see, target, or steer any context menu - it is invisible in argus.inspect while a human sees it on screen. This was proven live during MT-121 by tests/test_mcp_snapshot_viewport.rs::mt121_memory_backed_context_menu_remains_invisible_to_the_sized_capture_pass, which shows author_id 'ctx-menu.pane.pop_out' present in the rendered kittest frame and absent from the published snapshot. MT-121 fixed viewport SIZING only and deliberately did not fix this; the failing condition is asserted as current behaviour there, so that assertion MUST be inverted by this MT.

acceptance_criteria.text: A pane context menu that is open in the live window appears in the published MCP snapshot with its stable author_id, role and bounds, exactly as it appears in the rendered AccessKit tree.

The projection is general, not a hard-coded allowlist of one menu: any egui::Memory-backed surface the shell can open is projected into the capture context by a single documented mechanism, and adding a new menu does not require a new bespoke copy step.
Bounds published for the projected menu lie inside the declared SnapshotViewport and match the rendered frame, preserving the MT-121 coordinate contract.

The MT-121 test mt121_memory_backed_context_menu_remains_invisible_to_the_sized_capture_pass is inverted to assert the menu IS visible, and its comment is updated so it no longer documents the defect as expected behaviour.
A closed context menu is still absent from the snapshot: the fix must not make menus permanently visible, which would be a different falsehood.

PT-135-3: a negative proof that a CLOSED context menu does not appear in the snapshot.
PT-135-4: the full native lib suite still green (MT-121 baseline was 2069 passed / 0 failed).

target_entries: agent tool reference: which surfaces are visible to argus.inspect and which are not

risks: A blanket Memory copy could leak stale or half-open surfaces into the snapshot and make models act on a menu the operator already dismissed.
Copying Memory wholesale could import focus/scroll state that changes layout and breaks the MT-121 coordinate contract.
A per-menu allowlist would regress the moment a new menu is added, recreating this defect silently.
minimum_controls: AC-135-5 negative proof for the closed state.

independent_findings.detail: Commit 6be71449 (the only MT-135-tagged commit) modifies src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/knowledge.rs (numstat: 422	81	src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/knowledge.rs) which is outside allowed_paths [src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs, src/frontend/handshake_native/src/accessibility/, src/frontend/handshake_native/src/mcp/, src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/]. The only recorded out-of-scope waiver (lifecycle.out_of_scope_waiver_status_2026_09_02, GRANTED_BY_OPERATOR) covers src/frontend/handshake_native/src/manual_content_editors.rs only. A 400+ line backend storage-trait change inside a frontend capture MT is a clear scope spill, not an ancillary file.

The hunk converts required methods of `pub trait KnowledgeStore` into default bodies returning `Err(StorageError::NotImplemented("surreal knowledge edge backend"))`. At HEAD: 82 trait methods, 82 carry a NotImplemented default; 0 of those are NOT overridden by `impl KnowledgeStore for SurrealDatabase` (the only impl in the crate) and are therefore live placeholder error paths reachable from any caller of the trait: (none). This is the placeholder/hollow pattern CX-573D forbids in /src/ and the 'new placeholder error variant of the same shape' named by Spec-Realism sub-rule 1. `StorageError::NotImplemented` is used in 4 product files: src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/knowledge.rs, src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/mod.rs, src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/database.rs, src/backend/handshake_core/src/workflows.rs.

The backend hunk plausibly belongs to the same-day PostgreSQL-removal consolidation (4f92cc25 2026-08-16); the MT-135 contract records no justification for it. Re-attribution, if the Orchestrator chooses it, must be recorded in this contract; it does not remove F-135-V1-2 from the product tree.

No trait method may return a placeholder error on a live product path. The 0 currently un-overridden methods are the minimum list: (none).
